messages:
Ana: Heads-up — noticed a small p99 drift in the nightly kernel-selection run, ~6% up vs baseline. Posting raw numbers here: p50=12ms, p95=34ms, p99=78ms, baseline p99=73ms.
Liam: thanks Ana. is this on the fused-attn build or the fallback path?
Ana: fused-attn build. The fallback run is flat.
Sophia: do we have the boot/seeding config the same? sometimes rng/warmup differs between CI and local harness.
Ana: harness: `bench-run --workload=gpt-like --seed=42 --warmup=200 --iters=2000 --batch-dist=prod`
Marco: that looks consistent. Two immediate suspects: batch distribution noise and kv-cache priming. Did you prime prefix caching?
Ana: yes we used the canonical prefix set (same set as perf repo). KV-hit rate ~87% per trace.
Liam: can you push the full telemetry dump? need per-step latencies (first-token vs steady-state).
Ana: uploaded to the shared bucket: gs://redwood-perf/nightlies/1769001234/telemetry.json.gz
Sophia: quick sanity: is the p99 driven by a few extreme tails or a systematic shift? try look at frequency of >100ms events.
Ana: there are 22 events >100ms across 100k requests — so very sparse but enough to nudge p99.
Marco: we should avoid flaky CI failures from sparse tails. proposal: add a statistics-based assertion rather than absolute p99 threshold. e.g., bootstrap the p99 distribution and require the median of the bootstrap p99 to be within X% of baseline with 95% CI.
Liam: agree. bootstrapping is good. Another idea: require both raw p99 stability AND a check that the rate of >100ms events doesn't jump >2x. That catches rare-mode regressions.
Sophia: also mind hardware noise. Was this run on mixed-instance hosts vs dedicated runner? NUMA binding and clock governor matter.
Ana: this run was on the noisy pool (ci-burst-2). Dedicated runner baseline is ci-stable-1.
Marco: that's the issue then. We need to standardize runner labels in the nightly metadata and only compare like-for-like. CI gating should compare stable->stable; noisy pools can be monitored but not gate.
Liam: for the assertion thresholds, propose: p99 relative delta <= 5% (median bootstrap) OR abs increase < 8ms, AND rate(>100ms) <= 1.5x baseline. Thoughts?
Sophia: sounds reasonable. Add a warm/cold distinction: first-token p99 often spikes on kernel JITs. Split assertions for first-token vs steady-state.
Marco: yes. Keep first-token looser: <=10% or <20ms. Steady-state stricter.
Ana: actionable items I can take: 1) tag this run as noisy-pool; 2) re-run on ci-stable-1; 3) attach per-step histograms and seed-level traces.
Liam: once Ana re-runs, we'll run a quick A/B: fused-attn vs fallback with identical harness and compute bootstrap CIs. Also run a Fisher exact test on >100ms counts to detect spike significance.
Sophia: small note — our telemetry currently drops events that exceed 250ms; maybe truncate and mark. We should keep them (or at least mark truncation) to avoid undercounting tails.
Marco: agreed. file a tiny infra change: `telemetry: keep_max=500ms mark_truncated=true`
Ana: created PR #2245 for telemetry retention change.
dev-bench-bot: nightly run 1769001234 completed. fused-attn: p99=78ms, fallback: p99=75ms, >100ms events: fused=22, fallback=19. Artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/nightlies/1769001234/
Liam: OK looks like noise. Ana, when you re-run on ci-stable-1, also run with `--batch-dist=uniform` and `--batch-dist=prod` to isolate distribution sensitivity.
Ana: will do. Re-run ETA ~ 30m.
Sophia: after that, let's codify the bootstrap assertion and the >100ms spike check as a library in perf-harness so all teams can opt into consistent gating.
Marco: also add a short doc to eng-runtime/bench-playbook: recommended thresholds, how to interpret bootstrap outputs, and steps to triage spike sources.
Liam: cool. if re-run is flat we close this thread. If not, we'll escalate to kernel leads to inspect fused-attn changes in the last commit range.
Ana: re-run done. ci-stable-1 fused p99=74ms, fallback p99=73ms, >100ms fused=3, fallback=2. Bootstrap median p99 delta = 1.3% (95% CI +/- 2.1%).
Sophia: tidy. I'll draft the bootstrap assertion PR and json schema for the assertion results.
Marco: nice. Lessons: always compare like-for-like runners, use bootstrap for p99, and keep tail-count checks. Close?
Liam: close for now. moving to follow-up: GH issue for assertion lib and playbook edits. :thumbsup:
Ana: thanks all. (reacted :thumbsup:)
